question: What is the least value of \(n\) such that \(n!\) is a multiple of \(2024?\)
solution:
The prime factors of \(2024\) determine which factors must occur in \(n!\). We have
\[
2024=8\cdot253=2^3\cdot11\cdot23.
\]
If \(n<23\), none of the integers from \(1\) through \(n\) has the prime factor \(23\). Their product \(n!\) therefore cannot be divisible by \(2024\).

For \(n=23\), the product \(23!\) contains the distinct factors \(8\), \(11\), and \(23\). Their product is \(2024\), so \(2024\) divides \(23!\).

Thus the least value is \(\boxed{23}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
